### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7715d049e4438f3b656c8d77a873871d38cf130e`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7715d049e4438f3b656c8d77a873871d38cf130e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2eddb435a4c9107475437c62f768287d1fc1cfe5` — the merge of head `313560aefa4483bddbd243e0092b937d16d4e5fc` into base `7715d049e4438f3b656c8d77a873871d38cf130e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2eddb435a4c9107475437c62f768287d1fc1cfe5 && git checkout 2eddb435a4c9107475437c62f768287d1fc1cfe5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7715d049e4438f3b656c8d77a873871d38cf130e 313560aefa4483bddbd243e0092b937d16d4e5fc && git checkout -B drift-repro 7715d049e4438f3b656c8d77a873871d38cf130e && git merge --no-ff 313560aefa4483bddbd243e0092b937d16d4e5fc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7715d049e4438f3b656c8d77a873871d38cf130e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7715d049e4438f3b656c8d77a873871d38cf130e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `313560aefa4483bddbd243e0092b937d16d4e5fc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-cap.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-grant-offer.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/delegated-admin-invite.dogfood.test.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.test.ts, packages/spec/scripts/check-error-code-provenance.ts, .changeset/23945-invite-role-cap-codes.md, .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/ci.yml

Inputs: card #23945 (body; comments `6217250590`, `6226340273`, `6226946317`, `6228142342`, the claim `6243550870`, the dev report `6244087940`); #24082 (body; comments `6226978922`, `6227435484`, `6227800739`, `6228134436`) and its contract review `6227714971`; PR #24238 (body, eight-file list, net diff `6e43b7bc3f..313560aef`, where `6e43b7bc3f` is the merge-base with `origin/main`); the head's check-runs, read at 2026-10-18T01:44Z. Everything was read with `git show` / `git grep` at the sha and unauthenticated REST GETs. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the two `scripts/pm/` tools this record is rendered and posted with are not gates. better-call is not installed in the read tree, so its body pass-through was not re-read (bound declared in ①).

### ① Derived judgments

**Gate verdicts on this head (41 check-runs, all completed).** 35 are success, 6 are skipped by their path filters or opt-in (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the sharded `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`), none failed, and none was still in progress after a bounded wait (the six `Test Core` shards and `Type Check · workspace` reported last). All five required contexts are success: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. The gates this change rests on, each success: `check:error-code-casing`, `check:error-status-conformance`, `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` and `check:error-code-provenance` (lint.yml `Lint · docs & code guards`, :2807, :2824, :2845, :2864); `check:docs` (`Type Check · source gates`); `check:api-surface` (`Type Check · consumer gates`); the per-package typechecks of plugin-auth, spec and dogfood (`Type Check · workspace`); the unit pins (`Test Core`, six shards); `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` (ci.yml `Build Core`, :2699 and :2723 — the one family the dev could not measure locally); `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · ESLint`. One bound on what these verdicts cover — the dogfood wire pins — is declared at the end of this section.

**The ledger hunk changes no accept-set, and it is the whole schema face of this PR.** The hunk is −4/+3, every line a comment, inside the `'@objectstack/plugin-auth'` array between `INVITE_EMAIL_FAILED` and `INVITE_REQUIRES_EMAIL`. No row is added, removed, renamed or moved; `STANDARD_SYNONYM_WAIVERS`, `PROVENANCE_WAIVERS` and the standard catalog are untouched. `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` feeds `REGISTERED_ERROR_CODES` and then `ErrorCode`, and all three accept exactly the strings they accepted before. The generated reference pages carry bare names only, so no regeneration is owed; `check:docs` (success) and `check:api-surface` (success, "public API surface + factory signatures unchanged") agree. `reviewFace` on the eight paths returns this one file as the schema hit; the other seven are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, read here only where the ledger comments make a claim about them. Right.

**Each comment against its emitter, read in the cited code.** The producer is `invitationRoleCapFailure` (`invitation-role-cap.ts` :182–:230). It still has exactly three non-null returns, each now an object with its own constant: :198–:207 (`INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED_CODE`, on `GRADE_UNRESOLVED`), :211–:219 (`INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_ISSUER_CODE`, the grant table does not admit and the requested grade outranks the issuer's) and :221–:229 (`INVITE_ISSUER_MEMBER_ONLY_CODE`, the remainder, reached only by an issuer below admin grade because `grantTableAdmits` :162 refuses every non-admin). Its one caller is still `beforeCreateInvitation` (`auth-manager.ts` :3524–:3531), which throws `new APIError('FORBIDDEN', { message: refusal.message, code: refusal.code })` — 403 with the code in the body, the shape `remove-member` already uses in the same file (:7700–:7706) and the vendor's `owner` refusal on this door arrives in (the card's table).

| Row | The comment says | The code at this head | Verdict |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `INVITE_ROLE_ABOVE_ISSUER` | 403: the requested role grades above the issuer's own | :211–:219, thrown 403 at :3530 | matches; wire-pinned (dogfood, a `delegated_admin` inviting `admin`) |
| `INVITE_ISSUER_MEMBER_ONLY` | 403: an issuer below admin grade may invite only as `member` | :221–:229, thrown 403 at :3530 | matches; wire-pinned (dogfood, a `delegated_admin` inviting `delegated_admin`, new case) |
| `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` | 403, fail-closed: the read answered with no usable row, or the composition has no data engine; a read that throws answers `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (503) instead | :198–:207 on `GRADE_UNRESOLVED`; `resolveMembershipRole` (:7866–:7888) returns `null` on missing keys (:7872), no engine (:7874) and no usable row (:7887); its `catch` (:7880–:7882) now throws `invitationRoleCapReadFaultApiError`, which is `APIError('SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', { message, code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE' })` (:1369, :1383–:1394) | matches; unit-pinned three ways (`auth-manager.test.ts` :1275 no row, :1291 no engine, :1303 a thrown read answers 503 and not the refusal's code) |

The missing-keys exit (:7872) is still not named by the comment, exactly as the #24082 review accepted: better-auth hands the hook a session user and an organization, so an invitation that reaches the hook cannot practically produce it. The reworded block comment — "each thrown 403 from `beforeCreateInvitation` with its code (#23945)" — is true at this head and the text it replaces ("today the cap throws a bare `FORBIDDEN`") would be false after landing; the contract file must not describe a producer that no longer exists. Right.

**The row-to-emitter link is now compiler-checked.** The three constants are typed `RegisteredErrorCode` (`invitation-role-cap.ts` :74–:78, a type-only import from `@objectstack/spec/api`, a subpath spec exports and plugin-auth already imports in two other modules). A removed or misspelled ledger row therefore fails plugin-auth's `tsc`; the dev's reverse verification (`TS2820`) is the expected shape of that failure. This is stronger than the value pin in `error-code-ledger.test.ts` alone, and it is the right direction: the ledger stays the one source, the emitter cannot drift from it silently. The provenance gate (`check-error-code-provenance.ts`, the `constdef` pattern at :134, `const NAME: Type = 'X'`) sees the three definitions as plugin-auth stamp sites, and plugin-auth's owner key lists all three → success. `INVITATION_ROLE_CAP_READ_FAULT_CODE = 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'` (:1369) is a `StandardErrorCode` member (`errors.zod.ts` :113), not a registered row, so it is outside that gate's population and inside the dispatcher vocabulary's; `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` success. Right.

**The 503 split (option B of #24082's open question 1) is right, and the card decided it on the record.** Four grounds: the #21941 rule in the same file — a read that could not answer is not a verdict, so it must not wear the refusal's words — applied at the one place the two were merged (`catch { return null; }`, the cap's own read, one caller); the status is the standard member's own (`HttpStatusErrorCodeMap` 503 → `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `errors.zod.ts` :195), so `check:error-status-conformance` has nothing new to reconcile and passed; fail-closed holds by construction — the throw leaves the hook before better-auth writes `sys_invitation`, and the hook wraps the read in no `catch` (:3524–:3527); and the body carries `code`, so after this PR every answer the cap gives on `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member`, refusal or outage, has one — the card's own "Expected" sentence. The verdicts do not move: the parity grid in `invitation-role-grant-offer.test.ts` (more than a hundred cells, the oracle's admit/refuse logic unchanged, now `toEqual` on `{ code, message }`) pins branch → code as well as admit → `null`.

**Public surface of `@objectstack/plugin-auth`: unchanged.** `src/index.ts` is `export *` over named modules; `invitation-role-cap.ts` is not among them, `auth-manager.ts` carries no `export … from` line, and the tsup entries are `src/index.ts` and `src/rate-limit-storage.ts` only. So `INVITE_*_CODE`, `InvitationRoleCapRefusal` and the changed return type are internal, and `resolveMembershipRole` is `private`. The other two importers of the cap module (`adopt-membership.ts`, `last-admin-guard.ts`) take `orgRoleGrade` / `parseOrgRoles` / `isOrgAdminGrade`, none of which changed. The PR body's zero-occurrence count on the built `.d.ts` is the dev's reading (`dist` is not built here); it is consistent with the source.

**Bounds declared.** (a) The pass-through of `code` from `APIError`'s body to the wire was not re-read in better-call; it stands on the `remove-member` precedent in the same file, on the vendor's `owner` refusal arriving with `code` through the same class, and on the dev's wire reading at this head (`body.code` for both reachable codes). (b) The dogfood wire pins did not run on this PR: the dogfood matrix is `main`'s full battery, the `filter` job skipped the three shards and the `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregate passes on a legitimately skipped matrix by design. So those two pins are measured by the dev's local run (`Tests 5 passed` at this head) and by `main`'s battery after landing, not by these check-runs. The unit pins run under `Test Core`.

### ② Semver level

**`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` with `Clause-②: no` and no arm, in both carriers (PR body and changeset) — matches what ships.** plugin-auth is published (`publishConfig.access: public`) and its `dist` changes, so a changeset is owed and present; a fix in a released package takes `patch` (Post-Task Checklist #3). Not `yes`: no accept set widens (the same invitations are admitted — the grid pins it), no public face widens (the three codes were registered at #24082, where the `minor (widening)` was paid; emitting a registered code widens nothing), and no export is added. Not `(narrowing)`: the 403 → 503 on a thrown read is a status correction on an outage path, not a published accept set made smaller; the standard code it answers with already existed. `@objectstack/spec` owes nothing — comment-only, `ErrorCode` unchanged, `check:api-surface` success. `@objectstack/dogfood` is private. `Check Changeset` is success, and the two gates that read the `Clause-②` line (`check-changeset-no-major`, `check-adr-0087-registration`) run in `Lint & Repo Gates`, success. The changeset's three meaning lines agree with the ledger comments; its `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` line names the no-row and no-engine inputs and its 503 paragraph names `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and the slug-guard precedent, so the CHANGELOG text stays true. Its closing "the status of every refusal (`403`)" is true because the outage is not a refusal, which the sentence before it says.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev deviations** (`6244087940`, seven), each answered:
1. **The block comment above the three rows was reworded too.** Accepted. Same file, same rows, comment-only; the claimed surface was the `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED` comment, and the #24082 review's point (b) asked for exactly this narrowing in the landing that splits the fault. The old text would have been false. This file is the scope floor of this review, read whole.
2. **`invitation-role-grant-offer.test.ts` edited.** Within the claim's "plugin-auth's own tests beside the cap"; the return type forced it, and the grid now pins more, not less. Accepted.
3. **The 503 body carries `code`; the slug guard's does not.** Accepted as the right direction — every answer on this door now has a code. The slug guard's codeless 503 is the gap, escalated below.
4. **`origin/main` moved after the branch point and was not merged in.** Measured: `git diff --stat 6e43b7bc3f origin/main` over the eight paths is empty, and over `packages/spec/src/api` and `packages/plugins/plugin-auth` whole is empty (seven commits now). The PR's CI ran on the merge ref; the queue re-verifies. Accepted.
5. **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally.** Answered on this head: it runs in ci.yml `Build Core` (:2699, with `check:lean-entry-closure` at :2723), success.
6. **A probe file was created and deleted.** The eight-file list carries no probe file and the branch is one commit. Accepted.
7. **The attribution trailer.** The commit ends `Claude-Session:` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude` with no model identifier; the PR body's footer is the session-URL form; no model identifier anywhere in the diff. Accepted.

**`open_questions`: none declared.** Right: the four points #24082's review handed over are each decided in the PR body, and this record agrees with the decisions (next).

**#24082's four points to this card (`6228142342`), each read:**
1. **Settle the split.** Settled B, on the record, with the ledger comment narrowed in the same landing and the spec path declared in the claim as a spec-lane surface. Right.
2. **Place the no-engine exit.** Fail-closed as `INVITE_ISSUER_UNVERIFIED`, pinned (`auth-manager.test.ts` :1291), named in the ledger comment, and reachable only by a bare `AuthManager` built without `dataEngine` (`AuthPlugin` hard-depends on the data service). "Cannot check" is never "does not apply". Right.
3. **Re-measure path :175 (now :198).** Measured on the wire: a non-member with a session gets better-auth's own 400 `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`, a plain member its 403 `YOU_ARE_NOT_ALLOWED_TO_INVITE_USERS_TO_THIS_ORGANIZATION`, both before the hook. So the code has no public-door input short of a race or a role-less row. The row stays — it ships in `dist` and is therefore registered (#16404), and the unit pin at :1275 records the reason in its comment. Accepted. One non-blocking note: the ledger row's own comment names the two inputs but not this reachability reading; a later ledger touch may add the one clause.
4. **The rows now have an emitter.** The producerless window closes at landing; nothing is owed. Right.

**Escalated to the owning seat, non-blocking** (this review has no GitHub write beyond this comment):
- **(a) The organization slug guard's 503 body carries no `code`** (`slugGuardReadFaultApiError`, :1356–:1366, `update-organization`). That is the same defect class this card was filed for, on another public door; by Prime Directive #10 and the card's own filing standard it is a card (p3 at most), not an acceptance note — "no public door produces a store fault on demand" describes the repro's cost, not the defect's status. Carrier: the services seat files it.
- **(b) `error-code-ledger.test.ts` :234–:237** keeps the comment "a bare `FORBIDDEN` today" and the case name "registered ahead of their plugin-auth producer"; both become history at landing, while the pin itself (value, owner key, synonym gate) still holds. A spec-lane comment-only follow-up, outside this PR's claimed surface. Carrier: the spec seat, on its next ledger touch.
- **(c) `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json`** could score the admin-role refusal by code. Carrier: the checklist's owner.

**Landing.** No governed surface is touched (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success), so the queue needs this PASS record for the schema face plus every required context green. At the read time above every check-run had completed and every required context is success, so the owning seat may ready and arm this PR on this record; the queue re-verifies on its rebuilt generation, and the two dogfood pins are read on `main`'s full battery after landing.
